note: An operator's notice: `json` is the file an operator writes; `canonical` is hoi_types::NodeNotice::canonical (DAG-CBOR, one-letter keys, optional fields left out when empty), hashed with BLAKE3 into `hash`; operator `o`, contact `c` and country `k` are always written and may be empty, since an operator may leave who and where out. A public node sends both in its hello to strangers (`nh`, `nt`) and puts the canonical bytes in its node link (`n` in the masked code), with the endpoint key's Ed25519 signature over `statement` (`s`); the earlier clear-text link spelled them `nt=` (deflated) and `ns=`, and `legacy_link` still opens. Clients show the notice before they say anything of their own.

pieces.note: The same notice from a node that keeps encrypted pieces for others (`hoi-node --hold-pieces`): `s: true` is added and the fixed sentence hoi_types::notice::PIECES shows after what the node processes. Older readers ignore the key; the hash covers it.
pieces.text:
Join notice – sleepy-walrus-48213

Operator. This node is operated by Lena. Contact: lena@example.org.

Server location. The server is located in XX and hosted by Example Hosting.

What this node processes. To connect you with communities, this node processes your IP address, connection times and technical connection data. Nothing beyond that: the node keeps the open communities it carries (their posts and media, which are public) and the addresses of the other public nodes it reached.

Encrypted pieces. This node also keeps encrypted pieces of posts and encrypted messages of private communities for other people's devices, and hands them back when asked. It cannot read them. Each is deleted when it expires, after 400 days at most.

Logging and retention. IP addresses are logged for 7 days for security and abuse prevention, then deleted.

Purpose. The data is used only to operate this node and the communities it carries. It is not sold or used for advertising.

Other participants. Members of a community can see your IP address through direct peer-to-peer connections. The operator cannot control what they do with it.

Beyond this node. This node is one way into the network, not the only one. When you join a community, open an invite or a link, read, post, reply or sync, your device may also connect to other nodes and participants anywhere on the internet that carry those communities, and which ones changes over time. Public nodes that carry a notice show you theirs before your device tells them anything about you; participants' devices, and nodes without a notice, show none.

Your rights. You can ask the operator what data about you this node holds and request its deletion via the contact above.

Notice version ca66cb380a78, last updated 2026-11-03.
